notes.title: NorbSoftDev GitHub
notes.notes:
We've decided that it makes more sense to post our sdk files on github rather than ship with the game.  It's easier to find the files and you can use the source to modify the program to your needs.  For the workshop tool there is a ./bin folder that contains the built program.

You do have to have a steam_appid.txt file in order to run the program.  That file contains the steam app id of the target file.  So for GB, you put in one appid, for WL another.  We've also included the two sample files, so it should be pretty easy.  It's a very basic program and I think it's based on other examples we've seen.

We also are putting our AI source and our other SDK tools here.

notes.title: Resolution
notes.notes:
We just heard back from Steam and the GB DLC is no longer able to be purchased.  We've addressed the issues and that they cannot be solved.  The same content and remastered game is now available through the GB Standalone product.  It really is exactly the same which is what caused so many issues.  We promised we'd deliver it as a DLC and we promised that we'd deliver it as a standalone.  We did, but we did not take into account how well Steam would handle what we were trying to do.  Really, why should they?  It was my crazy plan.

We will have the stand alone on sale again if you missed the wargamer sale.  But the good news is that you should be able to get a refund for the DLC now.  So please do as soon as you can.

Now that this is over we are working on moving forward and fixing any remastered issues.

NOTE that both games use the same engine.  They will both get the updates.  All future plans to expand features will affect both games.

The really cool thing is that you can also download the original 'classic' version if you want.

Thank you for your patience,
(I always laugh at that as I am not patient and when people say that you really did not have much of a choice)

notes.title: That Didn't Work
notes.notes:
The Gettysburg DLC did not go as planned.  Our testing, our planning ignored one major area that is a no go.  Can Steam support what we are trying to do.  It cannot.  I'm not blaming it on anyone but me and our team.  We should have caught this and known before we released.

Our plan was to put GB as DLC for WL and WL as DLC for GB.  So no matter which path you choose, you can get what you want.  We tried to be everything to everyone and it failed miserably.  Soon after launch players pointed out these issues and research showed that there was no good solution.

In our testing we were just trying to get everything working.  We mostly tested the DLC, as the stand alone game would be the same engine.  We got everything working at the last hour.  But just did not spend enough time integration testing.  Even with all that there are still bugs we missed and it sucks.  But all we can do is own up to them and fix them.  We cannot move forward until we have the solid base. 

Two apps cannot share the same workshop, so all mods would have to be copied and supported in two areas.  The same issue comes into play in the game lobby.  Although there may be a hack for it, it could get shut down in the future.  So GB DLC could not MP against GB stand alone and that's not acceptable.

The only solution that solves these issues is to discontinue the GB DLC, give everyone a refund.  I've already requested this from Steam and am waiting to hear back.  I cannot shut down the store right now or change it.

We apologize that this happened and we are trying to make it right as quickly as possible.  Thank you to everyone who jumped on this and found these issues very quickly.

notes.title: Almost There!
notes.notes:
Last year we made some promises to our players.  We said that there would be a big sale on the price of GB.  We said that the same engine would run GB and WL.  We said that even if you bought WL first, you'd be able to buy GB as DLC.

I wish I could take all that back, but I can't so we did it.  It would have been much easier to just have the two separate games, or just one game.  But I have a big mouth and we all like to do what ever we can to say thanks to everyone for supporting Scourge Of War.

We initially moved to Steam to take advantage of their MP and Lobby system.  We did that.  We also got both games out fairly quickly.  This last step of completely moving GB to the new engine has been tough.

We will be releasing it all towards the end of the month and it will be greatly discounted, as we promised.

We only hope we don't miss too many issues.  There will still be some tweaking involved in completely porting the AI.

notes.title: Dev Update 20241026
notes.notes:
The two biggest projects in converting GB to the remastered engine are the screens and the AI.  Looking back on how I did the AI dll, I'm not very happy with the work.  It's very limiting and hard to understand.  I am looking to redesign the interface as doing the same for GB is just building on a crumbling tower.

The concept of the AI is to receive the information and then issue a series of commands.  It should be simple.  The first pass I just moved code from the main engine to a dll and it caused a ton of odd functionality.

The forced checks should not happen in the AI.  Meaning the forced fallback, retreat, and route are not AI routines.  They are engine rules and therefore should not be moddable.  But other items, such as the full strategic AI should be included in the DLL rather than the odd mix that is there.

The design concept that I am striving towards is where machine learning, behavior graphs, reinforcement learning, could be added if someone wanted to take on that project.  Those require a clear set of commands.  So you enter the AI routine and you send back a series of commands.

Of course if you really wanted to add true machine learning, you'd need to run it a LOT in order to train your model.  That's also not really possible and the game is not conducive to that feature.  But I can set it up that way so that it will be easier to add when we have the time.

I really hoped to get this done by the end of the year, but I'm not so sure at this point.  That is still my goal, so hopefully I can get there.

PS - Americans, go vote!

Norb

notes.title: Dev Update 9/10/2024
notes.notes:
MP saves.  That's been the bane of my existence (besides trolls) for the past few weeks.  Made significant progress yesterday and was able to send the 33MB saved game across the wire during setup.

A long time ago Mitra created a way to do MP saves.  It was a hack, but it did work if you set it up correctly.  Everyone can thank him that we're even doing this as it was never part of the original plans.  I had to ask the rest of the team how it even worked.

He created an ini file that had the name of a saved game.  So the scenario loads, everyone picks their officer, then the same saved game is loaded by everyone at startup.  The issue is that you have to get the saved game to everyone and they have to have the scenario and setup the ini file correctly.

I've taken that and changed it a little.  Now if you save MP games, it creates a saved game in the NetServ folder.  That's the folder we use to launch MP.  On setup that folder is sent to every player.  So we included the saved game (if it exists) as part of that exchange.

My test was that I saved the MP game.  The restartMP.sav was created in the NetServ folder.  I left the game, copied that folder.  I then selected the copy as the scenario for the next game, and it worked!

To those that do not care about the details...  MP saved games will be a new folder under the documents/sowx64/scenarios folder.  You cannot use the NetServ folder name, as that's the staging area.

As far as the MP error we the 'too much data' etc. errors from the Steam network library.  I think we have those beaten as well.  Looking at the long initial MP game launch now.

We have a few other improvements coming along nicely.  Not sure of an exact date yet, but hopefully soon.

notes.title: Thank You from NorbSoftDev
notes.notes:
Thank you for the great engagement of the upgraded games.  We we not sure that the community would welcome it, but it's nice to see we were wrong.  We've had great engagement and it's good to see these niche games still have a good audience.

There are so many cool features we want to add, but we're always playing catch up.   I have way too much on my plate and the team is very small with limited engagement this time around.  So we're doing what we can and making sure to be consistent in what we promise.  It's confusing as getting GB out early caused no end of questions and confusion.  We will do everything we have stated though.

It's a quiet time now on Steam, but starting in Autumn begins a lot of sales and we'll be fully participating.  We hope that will expose us to a larger player base.  Which in turn we hope will allow more competition in the MP lobbies.

Currently we have the Ligny and Wavre in the Steam review process.  It's taking a while due to some confusion on requirements.

Once we get everything caught up we do have a list of new items to add to the game engine that we really feel will add new playability.

Thank you from NorbSoftDev!

notes.title: Dev Update 08/29/2024
notes.notes:
Wanted to just give everyone an update as we've made some promises and we're doing our best to make sure that we get everything covered.  We released GB early for those that could not wait.  It's basically the old version with a few critical upgrades.  There will be continued work on GB as we get to the point where we can use the remastered engine and can also release GB as a new DLC.

It's all confusing, but no matter what path you follow to get the games, we'll do our best to make sure that your faith in our small team is not misplaced.

Currently I am working on a form of MP saves.  A while back Mitra designed a sort of a hack to get something working.  It does work!  But it's a pain to get working.  I'm working on taking his idea and making it easier to enact.  In it's simplest form, it adds a saved game with the scenario that is sent to all the players.  So everyone loads the scenario, then the saved game, and hopefully we'll have the ability to restore MP.  We'll have to see if we can get some sort of autosave in there as well so that in the worst case where the game fails, you can recover.  It really sucks to play and setup for hours and then lose everything.

The biggest issue we see right now with MP is having different mods enabled.  This is also something I'll be taking a look at.  Many mods don't matter, it's trying to understand which is which that causes issues.  If you like using a modded toolbar in your MP games, you should be able to use it.  But we cannot allow anything that can upset the balance of the game.  It's always a balancing act trying to figure out which is which and we know (based on feedback) that we do not have it correct yet.

After these items are complete, I'll move to the GB AI and converting it to the dll format of the remastered version.   The rest of the team is working on updating the maps and the screens.  It's a large project, but when it's done GB will be remastered as well.  Yes, a campaign map for GB too!!!

We hope to have this done by the end of the year so that we can join the end of year sales and have two products that are indicative of SOW Quality.  We hope that by joining the sales we can get some front page time for increased exposure to more of the wargaming community.

Currently we are getting the other two DLCs for Waterloo finished (Wavre & Ligny).  Gettysburg workshop will have to wait until it's using the new engine as well as it's various DLCs.

We are also working on translations for everything!  English, Italian, German, French, Spanish, and Chinese.  We have some issues with the way we save some items and there are fixes that need to be made in order to support these features correctly.  I made the same mistake in languages and in the resolution.  Rather than save values, I saved indices.  Bad move.  So I plan on fixing that as well.  We are also looking at the font resolution issue and will have some solution for that in the future.  It might be something like 'large fonts' in where you can just globally increase the font size.

I think that's about it for now.  I hope we have at least a little of what's important to all our supporters.

notes.title: Gettysburg Is Released
notes.notes:
We have brought the GB store online and uploaded SOW Gettysburg and it's now for sale!  This was a little change of course for us and it took a while to figure out how to make everything work.  I think we have it finally.

When we brought Remastered for sale, there were many fans that asked for Gettysburg.  They had no interest in Waterloo, and just wanted the ACW and wanted it now.  Gettysburg has never been sold on Steam before, so it all made sense.  We just had to figure out how to do it with our goal of moving to just one game engine that can run everything.  

Gettysburg differs from Waterloo in the handling of AI, the user interface, and many of the file formats are different.  So the full conversion to the remastered engine will take some time.  So this is a step along the path, but know that if you are an ACW fan, GB is not done.  We will continue with improvements and will be eventually using the same engine for both games.

As a little taste we did bring some of the upgrades into the older engine.  A big performance boost as well as Steam multiplayer.   We also got it out as soon as we were able which was what we heard time and again.

Thank you again for the great community support!  It is a huge commitment upgrading these games with such a small team.  Thank you!

notes.notes:
Finally got the mod upload tool working.  We are going to work out the kinks and then we'll put it in the release for everyone to try.  Next step is having the game query the mods from the Workshop.  They are not put in the mods folder.

So....  If you have a mod, and you upload the mod, and you subscribe to that mod, then you will see it listed twice.  Once from the Mod folder and once from Steam Workshop.

This is going to be so cool!!!!!!!!!!

No longer will you have to search around for a mod.  No longer will you have to try and find a place to host a mod.  You can also vote on them, let the world know the best ones.

As Randy's Mod is probably the most famous one, we let him put his up first.  It was messed up, but it's there.  I finally got a good one up by posting one of MarkT's maps.

This has been a big hole in the game, where do I post and get mods.  Now it's answered and we're all excited to see all the mods in one place.

notes.title: Gettysburg Store Page is Live
notes.notes:
The store page for GB has just gotten approved this morning and it's now live.  This is the original GB offered again on Steam with the performance enhancements and Steam integration as Remastered.  Our goal is to eventually have only one engine driving the gameplay for all of our games.  It's a big project, so we wanted to get GB out there in the mean time.  We've had a ton of requests because GB has never been on Steam.   One thing we do promise is that our games for a battle will cost the same as the DLC for the battle.  So whether you buy GB as a game, or wait and buy it as a DLC for remastered, you'll pay the same price and get the same great features.

The Scourge Of War series has enjoyed an awesome community on Steam and the entire team is very excited to bring more great new features.  Steam has been excellent for development and we hope to integrate everything that makes sense.

NorbSoftDev is an indie game company that has been creating wargames for over 20 years.  The team is from all around the world and none are full time game developers.  They are wargamers from all walks of life and just share a love for the type of warfare from another time.  Scourge Of War is a game engine specifically created for regimental based warfare and completely moddable and unlimited as to what you can create by only your imagination.

notes.title: Dev Diary 20240729
notes.notes:
So we're facing a huge dilemma here.  Our goal was to have every game use the same engine, but when we really got down to taking a look at it, we realize that it would take a long long time.

First all of the screens need to be converted to MyGUI, which is a great goal, but a lot of work.  That work would add a lot of time to the project and we know for a fact that there are a lot of players that want GB now!

Second is that there have been a ton of changes in the engine, which means that it might not play the same.  Syncing the AI will also take time.

The other option is to release it as it's own game, going back on all we've been saying.  Bringing the critical updates into the GB engine.  The worst thing about that is that the screens only support one language.  This can be done over time, but we are trying to figure out the best answer for right now.

64 bit support
Async support
Steam lobby support

That we could deliver a ton faster.  The price would be the same, whether as a DLC for our current release or as a new game makes no difference.

#define VERSION_NUM "1.0107"

We've began beta testing. Found some bugs, fixed them, still testing. This is how it works:

MP button will bring you right into the lobby screen.
You have to join or create a room in order to see anyone
Who ever created the room is the server
If the creator leaves, next person becomes the owner
Room disappears when everyone leaves

Owner hits the "enter staging room" button
everyone is notified that the server has started
just wait and when it's up you will join the game
once the server starts, the room is locked down (can't join again so don't leave)
once you are connected, you leave the lobby

now you are on the regular MP setup screen and all should work as it has in the past

This is the ONLY way to do MP now. Sorry if you like direct IP, but it really sucks with firewalls. This way will work to allow you to play with ANYONE connected to Steam. It's very cool how easy it is to connect. All packets are routed through the Steam client, so there's no worries.

It's probably buggy, but it does work.

notes.title: Dev Update 20240725
notes.notes:
Thank you for all the support on our boards and on discord.  We really appreciate it and even the criticisms have a ton of value for our early access.

I have this standing desk at home, but I also have 5 dogs and 2 cats.  So everyday around noon, I look down and all I see is fur as the dogs like to sleep right below me.  There's an entire room, a couch, chairs, but they have to be touching my legs.  I can't put the desk lower because then I'm running over tails or having my girl Dixie interrupt me to go out every few minutes as she eyeballs a terrorist (in the shape of a Squirrel) running out back.  She has somehow learned to put her snout under my mouse hand and continues this until I get up.  Amazing her ability to get her way by preventing me from working until I take care of her.  I'd admire her effort if she didn't do it so often.  Right at my feet is Ejay, our latest re-homing effort.  Sounds cute right?  He's a Great Pyrenees and even as a puppy he's over 90 pounds.  I just have to slowly push him out of the way, nothing wakes him up.

I finally got the MP connection where I've been striving for a while now.  The little details matter so much in coding.  I just have to clean up the screens and we can get it to our testers.  It worked perfectly as I was able to play a game between my two different routers.  One is behind a firewall, the other is not.  It's the connection I've been striving to beat for a while now.  No mapped ports, just Steam running and relaying the packets.  Rufus!!! (sorry my daughter has been watching drew barrymore romcoms this week).

That's why there is copy protection, that's why we always have to deal with this garbage.  Because some lowlife wants clicks and puts up a link to download what others pay for.  So if you do grab it, please thank them for all the garbage piracy software we all have to deal with every day.  They are the direct reason it exists. notes.title: Dev Update 7/23/2024
notes.notes:
I've got to figure out how to write these things without having to find a picture to go along with it.  Thankfully the team has a folder with screenshots, so I have some options.

I was on contract for a while with a crypto firm and they changed direction and ended the contract.  So I'm looking for my next gig, but also not wasting any time and going full time on MP while also interviewing.  Of course if we sell over 100k copies, then I'll do this full time, but we're pretty far away from that :)  No worries, it's always been a labor of love for the team.

I've discovered a few things in the past few years, I'm not a huge fan of the new versions of C++.  Maybe if I spent more time using it then things would be different.  I've never been one to create template, although I use them all the time.  But there is a point where the code is very hard to read and I've always been someone to read the code rather than the docs.  I've also spent a few years now learning cloud backend services coding in Go.  It's so EASY.  After decades of C++, writing micro-services let's you focus so much more on the architecture rather than the code.  It's been nice to add a new skill to my portfolio.

Not much of an MP update so far.  I have the lobby working.  Right now that will be the way, the only way, to launch MP games.  I had to take the Steam version and backfit it into our older PowerLobby feature.  But it's going well and it connects much better.  By doing it this way, the Steam Client acts as the intermediary for MP.  Now I am working hard to get the kinks out of the game launch.

I have a couple of routers at home, a vpn as well.  Using the lobby connection method works everytime in launching a game between my machines when they are not on the same lan.  The host list will pick up the lan games, but when I use the different routers, they can never see each other.  But they can create a room and play a game together through there.

I knew there was going to be a way to do this through Steam.  It's a big reason we went all in on Steam.  When we were with Matrix, they had to run the lobby server.  It was a horrible solution, but when power lobbies went down, we did not have any other choice.  It was awesome that they did that for us, but I'd rather not be dependent on a publisher for that service.  Yes, I know we are now dependent on Steam, but it's different.

Thank you everyone for being patient while we work through these issues.  It's this community that convinced us to give it another go and move the games to x64.

I appreciate all the great feedback and we all attempt to answer the questions on the discussion group here and our new discord channel.

notes.title: It's Finally Out
notes.notes:
Very happy to finally get it out.  We are much less intensity than earlier in our lives.  The older we get the more amazing it is that we released this game by our little team.  It's a ton of code, I'm not sure I could even do it again.  So now we are just modifying what we already created.  Adding the features we've always wanted and a lot of just getting things right.  If MP is not working for you, just open the ports.  If it still doesn't work, then please be patient.  We have plans to make it a lot easier using a different API from Steam.

We have enhancements for the maps.  We no longer have the 32 bit memory limits and we run a good bit faster.  Just a little to wet your whistle.  We really hope you enjoy our efforts.  I was also pleasantly surprised to see we had a German translation with others planned.

For those that have already played, hopefully the new eye candy will help you out.  For others, it's finally ready.

Big items to come, SOWGB as a DLC.  Enhanced MP.  Leaderboards and Lobby.  Just to list a few items.

Thank you from all the team.  It's all the players and the great feedback that brought us together to give it another go.

notes.title: We Are Close
notes.notes: We've submitted a build for release, but it got denied.  Since we do not have a typical client server architecture, they could not confirm the MP.  We tried to explain how it worked, that we've had the game this way on Steam before, and we're waiting for the response.  I apologize that it's not ready by our release date.  But please be assured we are doing what we can to get it out as soon as possible.  Even if we just have to remove some tags so that they can pass it, we will.  It's submitted again, so we are just waiting.  Thank you!

notes.title: Dev Diary May 18, 2024
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44768844/493029dfc6ffdea4d921faeccfd6de78deee3470.gif[/img]

Sorry for the completely unrelated image, but I was feeling nostalgic.  This is the very first time I ever put my game code out for the world.  The people on that team have done some pretty cool things.

So I was trying to debug why our uploaded version was crashing.  The logs said that it was missing sprites, so I put in the sprites, but it still kept crashing.  I have a staging folder and I was trying to launch from there and it crashed every time, as if I was doing nothing.  Thing is that it was Steam enabled, so as soon as I launched the game from the staging folder, Steam shut it down and launched the version in the Steam folder.  Talk about frustration!  But I finally figured out why I was a dope today.

In real life I got fired.  That was a shocker.  It was over the fact that I said from day 1 I would not commute more than 15 minutes.  They changed the HR policy and decided they did not care about the terms of my employment.  It happens to the best of us, but it really is a shock because it just destroys everything you thought you could depend upon.  You fight for your family and do what it takes to get the income coming in again.  So if you see any odd pictures of me...

But SOW is the subject here.  Between all the craziness that real life throws at you, we've been working to try and get something out that is a little different, runs a little better, and looks much nicer.  It's a work in progress, so it's early access.  We are just trying to get everything together and we'll have it up for sale.  We've had some changes on the team, but my right hand is back in charge.  Jim has taken the reigns again so you can be sure that everything will get done.  We'll get all the team listed for the credits as we've got some new faces and the old guard together.  We're not fast, but we do finish and if we're lucky we'll give you something you like and improve it enough or make enough promises for you to be happy.  We still have major work to get done, it's not close to where we want it to be, but we are a small team and would love the input of our supporters.

We are still thinking that June will be our release, so stay tuned sportsfans.

notes.title: DevLog April 1st
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44768844/5f0a12e29708fb507bf2ac5f72991c275ac4262a.jpg[/img]

Life is absolutely crazy!  You just never know what is going to happen or where things will end up.  I find myself with extra time as I have 3 months to find a new job.  So I am interviewing and trying to fix SOW bugs.  The main issue is around switching the guts of MP still.  It's been a headbanger, but I finally found the culprit today and it's a huge relief.  There is still cleanup, but this is the last bug that would prevent a wimpy early access release.

It's hard to not just rewrite everything, you really want to when you are looking at code you wrote many years ago.  It's just not practical though.  The first release will have just a few enhancements as we are really doing a port and removing a bunch of garbage no longer needed.  We hope to have many release as we move forward and full Steam support in every way that makes sense.

We hope for a June release, so keep your fingers crossed!

notes.title: Dev Log 20240128
notes.notes:
Working towards being more active in keeping everyone up to date of where we are currently.  We started last year with the goal of converting Scourge of War Waterloo into a full Steam release.  To us that meant replacing all the libraries that we use with Steam API where provided.  This was mostly seen in our MP library.  We started with a great lib called Raknet and I cannot thank them enough.  Now it's time to move on and we're ripping out the guts and shoving Steam Networking inside.  This is taking longer than we thought as we still work part time, although we've been doing it so long that a few are retired.

The Waterloo idea has moved on to Scourge of War Remastered.  A common SOW 64 bit game to run all of our content as we upgrade it.  That includes all of our battles eventually released as separate DLC to the main game.  We also have a lot of new content and my hope someday that a fantasy or scifi mod is created for everyone to try :)

We also plan on using the Steam Workshop for mods, removing our old copy protection, using Steam leaderboards, etc.  All in on Steam and very happy they provide so many tools.  I still remember decades ago when I was upset that I had to download Steam and have it running to play Half Life 2.  Now it's just time to grow up :)

We hoped to get it out earlier, but we moved the date back.  We plan to do early access as soon as we figure out how to do that.  We want to put it out there so people can play.  We understand that there is no way to buy the game currently, and we want that fixed.

Progress??  Today we got the client and server connected and into a game.  It's taken a while to get there, but we are there.  Trying not to mess up what works while still using the new guts.  We took a break, have not worked on the code for a few years, but we're getting back in there.  A bunch of grumpy old men trying to use the green reanimator liquid on a classic.

We had two choices, keep the game with our publisher until the sales slipped into the nether or reset the base and give it a new more workable base.  We hope you agree and support our choice.
